rationale: The parent question is receipt-backed; this update targets the registered gap and the mis-specified control it left behind. I request one successor fixed experiment (previous_id: ce33f7b508af4244883ac9c81a2a4696-experiment) that keeps the executed scenario, fixes the local-API control's identity/admission pairing, measures the window opened by the forged message in the target's own clock, and adds a second scenario in which the same peer-form message reaches a quorum-relevant follower before a real campaign, so the disruption consequence can be observed rather than argued. The harness ran natively in a scratch copy with the predicted events; the formal reading is deferred to the retained receipt.

scope.description: Two real three-voter RawNode groups in one process (voters {1,2,3}, CheckQuorum+PreVote, shared storage snapshot at index=10/term=1). Group A repeats the executed scenario (real election for node 1, real heartbeat tick, local-type control, real MsgPreVote from a real campaign, peer-form MsgForgetLeader, re-delivery of the identical pre-vote) and then advances the leader's logical clock by one tick so that its next real heartbeat repairs follower 2. Group B does the same until the pre-vote control, then forges the same message to the quorum-relevant follower and lets node 3's campaign complete with the grants actually produced, observing pre-vote, vote and leadership outcomes.
assumptions: A peer may deliver an arbitrary protobuf message type to the public inbound path RawNode.Step; raft's wire form is unauthenticated, so the module's own IsLocalMsg filter is the boundary in scope.

Ticks are the target's logical clock: leader ticks of 1 with HeartbeatTick=1 produce one heartbeat per tick, and no follower is ticked between measurements, so the follower's own election timeout never fires during the run.

In group B the same node (3) both delivers the forged message and campaigns; the shared node identity is used only to correlate the admission event with the result event, so the experiment does not claim that attacker and candidate must coincide.
Grants are returned to the candidate through the same public Step path; the incumbent leader is not fed the new leader's messages, so its own demotion is outside this bounded prefix.
excluded: Transport authentication and rafthttp behaviour, outside this module.
Whether the deposed leader eventually steps down once the new leader's messages reach it (not delivered here).

experiment.prefix: Build six real RawNode instances as two independent three-voter groups from MemoryStorage snapshots (index=10, term=1, voters {1,2,3}) with CheckQuorum+PreVote; run a real election for node 1 and replicate its term-2 entry in each group; tick the leader once and deliver the real heartbeat to each follower. Group A: deliver MsgCheckQuorum from node 3 (local-type control), deliver node 3's real MsgPreVote (under-lease control), deliver the peer-form MsgForgetLeader (From=3, To=2, no term), re-deliver the identical pre-vote, then tick the leader once more, deliver the next real heartbeat and re-deliver the pre-vote a third time. Group B: deliver the real MsgPreVote (control), forge the same message to node 2, re-deliver the pre-vote and feed its grant back to node 3, deliver node 3's resulting MsgVote to node 2 and feed its grant back, and record both nodes' leadership state. All observations come from the public Step/Ready/Advance contract and BasicStatus; each event is a CA_EVENT JSON line.
experiment.responsibility: The application must deliver inbound peer messages to RawNode.Step; the raft module owns which message types are acceptable from the network and owns the meaning of MsgForgetLeader as a local authority-state change, and it owns the lease rule that is supposed to keep followers from supporting a candidate while the leader is alive.

assertion.value: raft: cannot step raft local message

comparisons.description: Control: a genuinely local type from the same peer is still rejected by the inbound filter.
Control: the pre-vote is not granted while the lease holds.
Defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader must not be accepted by the inbound path.
Consequence: if the message was accepted, the follower must still not grant the identical pre-vote while the leader is alive.
Re-specified control: the same state change is produced by the local API on a follower with a live leader context (lead 1 -> 0), which is why the network path must not reach it.
Repair path: the leader's next real heartbeat (one leader tick with HeartbeatTick=1) restores the follower's leader context.
Window bound: once the leader context is restored, the identical pre-vote is ignored again, so the window opened by the forged message is closed by the next leader message.
Group B control: the quorum-relevant follower does not grant the pre-vote while the lease holds.
Group B defect predicate: the peer-form MsgForgetLeader is not accepted by the inbound path.
Group B consequence (pre-vote): after the accepted forgery the same request is granted.
Group B consequence (vote): the follower that was made to forget also grants the real vote that lets the candidate reach a quorum.
Group B disruption: an up-to-date candidate must not become leader at a higher term while the incumbent leader is still serving; a witness where node 3 is StateLeader is the violated case.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds the repair-path measurement (one further leader tick -> next real heartbeat -> lead restored -> a third identical pre-vote ignored again), re-specifies the local-API control with a heartbeat prerequisite that carries the same identity field as its result (the previous version was unknown because the heartbeat event had no 'node' field), and adds a second test function in which the forged message reaches the quorum-relevant follower before a real campaign, so the election consequence is observed. The earlier harness artifact is preserved in the fixed experiment of the parent.
